summary: This prospective observational study investigated the impact of laser photocoagulation on the macula in 34 patients with peripheral retinal degeneration and/or breaks. Ocular examinations, including optical coherence tomography (OCT), OCT angiography (OCTA), and multifocal electroretinography (mf-ERG), were conducted at baseline and 1- and 3-month post-treatment, revealing significant changes in macular thickness and function. The study found that laser photocoagulation induced foveal hypoperfusion, macular thickening, and prolonged implicit times, with macular thickening persisting up to 3 months, and identified correlations between laser parameters and macular changes.
